hard_case: The only test of the bad-number path is `is_err()`, which cannot tell the variants apart.

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: `let n: u32 = part.trim().parse().map_err(|_error| ParseError::NotNumber)?;` becomes `let n: u32 = part.trim().parse().map_err(|_| ParseError::Empty)?;`, and the test's inputs do not tell the two apart
not equivalent: `let n: u32 = part.trim().parse().map_err(|_error| ParseError::NotNumber)?;` becomes `let n: u32 = part.trim().parse().map_err(|_| ParseError::NotNumber).unwrap_or(0);`

reasoning: word_is_an_error passes for any error. Returning `Empty` instead keeps it green; swallowing the error to 0 makes `parse_sum("a")` Ok and fails it. Shape: error variant not pinned.
